scenes.headline: How an ordinary LLM is trained into a decision model
scenes.sub: A fresh head, soft labels, and one epoch of LoRA
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Barnaby! Decision models answer with a probability per option, never a sentence. Here's how Unsloth trains one from any language model.

scenes.text: Write the input and every question into one prompt, then train a small head to score each option from the model's hidden states.
scenes.say: The idea: put the input and every question into one prompt, and train a small head to score each option.

steps.say: A record is a state plus typed questions. All of it, options included, goes into one prompt.
The language model reads it once, with small LoRA adapters learning.
Average the hidden states over each question's words, and each option's words.
A fresh head lets options search the whole input, and lets questions attend to each other.
Out comes one probability per option. No word is generated.

items.text: Mix typed questions from public datasets
items.say: Build rows from typed decisions and a dozen public datasets.
Attach a random head, and LoRA adapters on the language layers.

items.text: Train on the teacher's soft labels
items.say: Train against the teacher's full probability spread for one epoch.

items.text: Fit a temperature on held-out rows
items.say: Then fit a temperature, so confidence means how often it's right.

scenes.title: The loss
scenes.text: loss = - sum( target x log softmax(logits) )

parts.say: The target is the teacher's averaged distribution, so an ambiguous case stays ambiguous.

parts.note: the head's scores, one per option
parts.say: This is the head's distribution over the options.
The loss is lowest when the two match, not when the model is most confident.

scenes.title: What the before number is
scenes.note: unweighted mean of three benchmarks, Qwen3.5-0.8B
scenes.say: The headline jump, twenty point seven to seventy four point three, starts from a random head, not the base model.

scenes.label: parameters in the head on the small model
scenes.say: The head has about twenty seven million parameters, and nothing projects onto the vocabulary. That's how it trains in four gigabytes.

scenes.text: A decision model is a classifier that reads its label set at request time, trained like one.
scenes.say: A decision model is a classifier that reads its options at request time. And it's trained like one.

recap: A fresh head scores pooled spans
scenes.say: One prompt, a fresh head over pooled spans, soft labels, then a temperature.
